chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us from his father, from Khalaf b. Hammad, from Abu'l Hasan al-Abdi, from Sulayman b. Mehran, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr b. Habashi, from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said:

No banner was advanced to fight against the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, overturned it and overcame its companions, and they turned back humiliated. And the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) did not strike anyone with his sword Dhulfiqar except that they perished. And when he fought, Gabriel fought on his right side, Michael on his left side, and the Angel of Death before him.

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Believers -- title of Imam Ali b. Abi Talib
key_terms.ذي الفقار: Dhulfiqar -- the famous double-bladed sword of Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: How did angels support Imam Ali in battle according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith is narrated from Imam al-Hasan (AS) about the invincibility of his father, Imam Ali, the Commander of the Believers (AS), in battle. It describes how every opposing banner was overturned by God, how no one survived a strike from his sword Dhulfiqar, and how the archangels Gabriel and Michael and the Angel of Death accompanied him in combat. This tradition reflects the Shia belief in the divine support granted to Imam Ali in his military campaigns during the early Islamic period.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us from his father from Khalaf b. Hammad from Abi’l Hasan al-`Abdi from Sulayman b. Mehran from Abi Ishaq from `Amr b. Habashi from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Abi Talib (as). He said:

No banner proceeded to battle against Amir al-Mu’minin (as) except that Allah defeated it [through him] and made him triumphant over its companions and made them turn back in shame. None struck by Amir al-Mu’minin’s sword, the dhulfiqar, prevailed. When he would fight, Gabriel would fight on his right side, Michael would be on his left side, and the Angel of Death would be in front of him.
